title: Consistent histories and the ultrametric on infinite tensor products
abstract: The consistent histories formulation of quantum mechanics assigns classical probabilities to sequences of coarse-grained events when the corresponding interference terms vanish. In finite models these terms generically need not vanish exactly, and their smallness alone supplies no asymptotic geometry on the space of histories. We construct such a geometry for histories that accumulate quantum records. When the normalized Dowker - Halliwell interference between two histories factorizes as the cumulative fidelity of their records, its decay is controlled by the accumulated squared Bures distance. In the infinite registration limit, the Kakutani - von Neumann dichotomy gives a sharp sector alternative: summable Bures defect yields weakly equivalent record sequences, whereas nonsummable defect produces orthogonal superselection sectors and vanishing normalized interference. The convergence exponent of the Bures defect defines a pseudo-ultrametric on histories. After quotienting its zero distance degeneracy, it becomes a complete ultrametric, requiring neither compactness of the outcome space nor continuity of the record family, and coincides with the gauge invariant sector metric $\tilde d$ introduced in \cite{LesTP}. Its value, the \emph{consistency rate}, has three equivalent interpretations: it is the sector separation metric, the polynomial growth exponent of the negative logarithm of normalized interference, and, by the Helstrom formula, the corresponding exponent of the negative logarithm of the minimum error probability for discriminating the cumulative records. Classical separation profiles determine the rate: positive long time mean defect gives the maximal value $δ=1$, while the borderline profile $d_m^2\asymp m^{-1}$ produces distinct superselection sectors at zero polynomial rate, $δ=0$.
summary: This paper establishes a novel, rigorous geometry for quantum histories by defining a complete ultrametric based on the rate at which accumulated quantum records become distinguishable. This 'consistency rate' ($\delta$) quantifies the transition from quantum superposition to classical probability, linking fundamental concepts like interference decay and quantum error bounds. It provides a powerful mathematical tool for understanding decoherence in the infinite limit.
main_problem: The paper develops a rigorous geometric framework for histories in quantum mechanics, specifically addressing how to assign classical probabilities to sequences of coarse-grained events when interference terms are considered in the infinite limit.
main_result: It constructs a complete ultrametric on the space of quantum histories, whose convergence exponent, the 'consistency rate' ($\delta$), has equivalent interpretations related to sector separation, interference decay, and minimum discrimination error.
method: The analysis relies on extending the consistent histories formulation using the infinite tensor product structure and analyzing the decay of the normalized Dowker-Halliwell interference, which is controlled by the accumulated squared Bures distance.
model_or_system: The model is the abstract quantum mechanical history space, formalized using an infinite tensor product structure to represent the accumulation of quantum records ($\Omega = (\Omega_1, \Omega_2, \dots)$). It compares this idealized infinite limit to finite-dimensional record packing constraints.
key_observables: Normalized Dowker-Halliwell interference, accumulated squared Bures distance, the consistency rate ($\delta$), and the minimum error probability for discriminating cumulative records.
important_parameters: The rate $\delta$ is determined by the asymptotic behavior of the per-step record defect $\{b_m\}$, which can follow power-law profiles $d^2m \propto m^{-s}$.
main_assumptions: The use of the infinite tensor product is an asymptotic idealization, which bypasses finite-size packing constraints encountered in physical, finite-dimensional systems.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the definition of the consistent histories formulation to analyzing the decay of interference via the Bures distance. It applies the Kakutani-von Neumann dichotomy to characterize the asymptotic structure, culminating in the definition and interpretation of the ultrametric consistency rate $\delta$.
why_interesting: It provides a deep mathematical tool (ultrametric geometry) to quantify the operational distinguishability between quantum histories, offering a rigorous framework for decoherence and the emergence of classicality in open quantum systems.
